title: Kitty Duterte to appeal SC dismissal of petitions challenging father's arrest --lawyer
summary: The camp of Veronica “Kitty” Duterte said Wednesday it will appeal the Supreme Court decision dismissing the habeas corpus petitions challenging the arrest of former President Rodrigo Duterte in…

blocks.text: The camp of Veronica “Kitty” Duterte said Wednesday it will appeal the Supreme Court decision dismissing the habeas corpus petitions challenging the arrest of former President Rodrigo Duterte in March 2025.
Lawyer Paolo Panelo Jr., counsel for the younger Duterte, said they will file a motion for reconsideration.

“Yesterday we received, with deep disappointment, the Supreme Court’s ruling dismissing the petitions for habeas corpus as moot, and declining to pass upon the legality of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s rendition to The Hague,” Panelo said in a statement posted on his Facebook account.

“With due respect, the decision effectively reduces the great writ of habeas corpus to a race to remove the person detained outside Philippine territory before the courts can act. We will file a Motion for Reconsideration,” he added.

On Tuesday, the SC dismissed the consolidated habeas corpus petitions challenging the former president's arrest, ruling that they have become moot and that Philippine courts can no longer enforce the writ since he is now in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC).

In separate petitions filed in March 2025, Kitty and her half-brothers Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte and Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte asked the SC to order the government to present Duterte before the High Court.
During the filing, Kitty was represented by Panelo and his father, former chief presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo.
The younger Panelo argued that the ICC arrest warrant cannot be used as the basis for the arrest and detention of the former president, claiming that it has no jurisdiction in the Philippines.
He added that the ICC may only exercise its jurisdiction if the country’s legal system is not functioning, stressing that the Philippine judicial system is working.
The Philippines withdrew from the Rome Statute, the treaty that established the ICC, in 2019 after the Hague-based tribunal began a probe into the Duterte administration's drug war.
Duterte is set to stand trial for crimes against humanity before the ICC starting November 30, 2026. —AOL, GMA News
